title: Help
subtitle: Definitions, formulas, and how to read every KPI on this dashboard

kpis.title: Cross Sell Ratio
kpis.purpose: Measures the success of cross-selling strategy and the depth of the business relationship with customers — how many customers were persuaded to buy more than one product category.
kpis.formula: Customers Who Bought >1 Category ÷ Active Customers × 100%

definitions.desc: Customers who purchased more than 1 product category within the measurement period (monthly, quarterly, yearly).
A customer who made at least 1 purchase transaction within the measurement period.

interpretation: A rising number means the cross-selling strategy is reaching more customers successfully.
A falling number means customers tend to buy only one product category.
benchmark: < 25% — Low (still relying on a single product)
25% – 40% — Fair (healthy baseline for an AIDC distributor)
> 60% — Excellent (strong customer engagement and product penetration)

kpis.title: Average Product Category per Customer
kpis.purpose: Measures purchase depth — the average number of product categories each active customer buys within a period.

definitions.desc: The accumulated number of unique product categories purchased by all customers within a period.
A customer who made at least 1 purchase transaction within the measurement period.

interpretation: A rising number usually indicates effective bundling, successful up-selling/cross-selling by the sales team, or stronger customer engagement.
The higher the number, the better the product penetration into the customer base.

kpis.title: Average Revenue per Existing Customer
kpis.purpose: Measures the economic value of retained customers and the effectiveness of retention and account-growth strategy — the average revenue generated from existing customers.
kpis.formula: Total Revenue from Existing Customers ÷ Number of Existing Customers

definitions.desc: The total revenue generated from existing customers within the measurement period.
A customer who already had a transaction history before the current period and is still purchasing during that period.

interpretation: A rising number shows increased value per customer — could be from up-selling, cross-selling, or higher order frequency/size.
A falling number may indicate declining purchases, partial churn, or price pressure.

kpis.title: Average Gross Profit per Existing Customer
kpis.purpose: Measures the profitability of existing customers — not just revenue, but the actual margin contribution generated.
kpis.formula: Total Gross Profit from Existing Customers ÷ Number of Existing Customers, where Gross Profit = Revenue − Cost of Goods Sold (COGS)

definitions.term: Total Gross Profit from Existing Customers
definitions.desc: Total revenue from existing customers minus the cost of goods sold (COGS) within the measurement period.
A customer who already had a transaction history before the current period and is still purchasing during that period.

interpretation: A rising number shows existing customers are becoming more profitable — could be from buying higher-margin products, better pricing, or improved cost efficiency.
A falling number may indicate excessive discounts, rising production costs, or a shift toward a lower-margin product mix.

kpis.title: High Margin Product Penetration
kpis.purpose: Measures how well the company drives sales of high-margin products — the percentage of active customers who bought products with a bigger profit contribution.
kpis.formula: Existing Customers Who Bought High-Margin Products ÷ Active Customers × 100%

definitions.term: Existing Customers Who Bought High-Margin Products
definitions.desc: The number of existing customers who made at least one purchase in a product category with gross margin above the company's defined threshold.
A customer who made at least 1 purchase transaction within the measurement period.

interpretation: A high number means the sales team successfully steered customers toward more profitable products.
A low number means customers still predominantly buy low-margin products.

kpis.title: Repeat Order Rate
kpis.purpose: Measures customer loyalty, experience quality, and retention strategy effectiveness — the percentage of customers who made a repeat purchase after a previous transaction.
kpis.formula: Customers Who Made a Repeat Order ÷ Existing Customers × 100%

definitions.term: Customer Who Made a Repeat Order
definitions.desc: A customer who made more than 1 transaction within the measurement period, or returned to purchase after a previous transaction.
A customer who already had a transaction history before the current period and is still purchasing during that period.

interpretation: A high number means customers are satisfied, recurring needs are being met, and the business relationship is strong.
A low number may signal issues with service, product quality, or post-sale engagement.

kpis.title: Customer Expansion Rate
kpis.purpose: Measures the success of account-growth strategy — the percentage of business value growth from existing customers through increased purchases, added product categories, or expanded transaction volume.
kpis.formula: Customers with Increased Revenue ÷ Existing Customers × 100%

definitions.desc: A customer who already had a transaction history before the current period and is still purchasing during that period.
An existing customer whose purchase value in the current period is higher than in the previous period.

interpretation: A high number means account management is effective and the customer relationship keeps growing.
A low number means customers tend to be stagnant, and account potential isn't fully tapped yet.

kpis.title: Dormant Customer Rate
kpis.purpose: Measures the level of customer inactivity and potential revenue loss from the existing customer base — the percentage of customers who used to be active but stopped buying within a certain time window.

definitions.desc: A customer with a prior transaction history who hasn't transacted again past the dormancy threshold (varies by business category — typically 3 months for retail, 6–12 months for B2B depending on the business cycle).
A customer who already had a transaction history before the current period and is still purchasing during that period.

interpretation: A high number means churn risk is rising and customer engagement is weakening.
A low number means customer retention is healthier and the business relationship is better maintained.

kpis.title: Dormant Customer Value
kpis.purpose: Measures the business value that is "held up" or at risk of being lost due to customers who are no longer active — the total revenue or potential gross profit lost from dormant customers.
kpis.formula: Total historical value (revenue/gross profit) from all customers who are dormant during that period

definitions.desc: A customer with a prior transaction history who hasn't transacted again past the dormancy threshold.
The average or total revenue that customer previously generated before becoming dormant.
The historical gross profit that customer previously generated.

interpretation: A high number shows a lot of customer value hasn't been successfully retained or won back.
A low number means the customer base is healthier and revenue-loss risk is smaller.

kpis.title: Customer Reactivation Rate
kpis.purpose: Measures the effectiveness of reactivation strategy and the company's success in recovering customers who had stopped transacting — the percentage of dormant customers who came back to transact.
kpis.formula: Dormant Customers Who Transacted Again ÷ Total Dormant Customers × 100%

definitions.desc: A customer who was previously dormant, then made at least 1 transaction again within the measurement period.
All customers who were in dormant status at the start of the measurement period.

interpretation: A high number means follow-up strategy, engagement, and win-back campaigns are working effectively.
A low number means customers are hard to recover, or the reactivation approach isn't hitting the mark yet.
